_meta.description: The queue a reviewer works through before anything in the Suggestion register is built, plus a log of decisions already taken. A decision is only recorded as taken when the owner states it; this file never assumes one. Each entry names the options, what each option commits the site to, and the cheapest reversible first step.
_meta.how_to_use: Read the question, pick an option, and record it in the log at the bottom with the date. Until then the site stays exactly as it is. Nothing in this repository acts on a suggestion automatically.

statuses.Open - needs your answer: Waiting on the owner. The site does nothing in the meantime.
statuses.Recorded: The owner has stated the decision and it is written in the log.

_meta.ported_00ba6c2e_2026_11_15: A parallel session (arena/bb85f073-zone4, PR #50) published a seven-row decision worksheet on its own suggestions.html with its own D-01..D-07 numbering, which collided with this register's D-01..D-07. Rather than drop either, its four items that were not already covered here (product confirmation, marketplace and tracking ID, authorised automation, measurement and privacy) are ported as D-13 to D-16 with their options and recommendations preserved verbatim in substance, and its other three items map onto existing rows: its D-04 pricing to D-02 and D-08, its D-05 economics to D-08 and D-09, and its D-06 editorial direction to D-03, D-06 and D-12. Its four unique open questions are ported as Q-16 to Q-19.

decisions.question: Do the three product links carry an Associates tag, or should the site stop describing them as earning links?

options.label: Tag the links and keep the earning claim
options.commits_to: Requires an Associates account. The three short links get replaced with tagged Special Links, the site keeps its disclosure sentence, and clicks become attributable.
options.reversible: Yes. Reverting to untagged links is a data change and a rebuild.

options.label: Keep the links untagged and relabel the calls to action
options.commits_to: The site keeps sending readers to the products but stops claiming it earns from them, because it cannot. The disclosure sentence would have to be withdrawn, which in turn affects every page.
options.effort: One template change plus a policy-page rewrite.
options.reversible: Yes, but withdrawing and re-adding the disclosure across 21 pages is the largest single visible change the site could make.

options.label: Do nothing yet
options.commits_to: The current inconsistency stays live: the site says it earns from qualifying purchases while carrying no tag.

decisions.recommendation: A, if an Associates account exists or can be opened. Failing that, B is the only internally consistent option; C is the one that looks worst to a careful reader.

decisions.question: Should the site pursue Creators API access so prices and ratings can be published?

options.label: Yes, work toward API access
options.commits_to: Enrolment, the qualifying-sales prerequisite, and a cached price and rating per product with a visible observation timestamp. Largest reader-value gain available.
options.effort: The prerequisite cannot be shortcut; the build change is small.
options.reversible: Yes, but a published price history cannot be un-published from a reader's memory.

options.label: No, stay a specification site
options.commits_to: Prices and ratings stay blank permanently. The site must then compete on something other than numbers, which is the testing route in D-06.

decisions.recommendation: A if the site is meant to sell; B is honest and cheap but leaves the reader's obvious question unanswered indefinitely.

decisions.question: What will the site say about who writes it and how?

options.label: Name the human reviewer and describe the pipeline
options.commits_to: A named person becomes responsible for the copy. That person must actually read it before each publish.
options.effort: One editorial note and a review step in the process.

options.label: Describe the pipeline without naming a person
options.commits_to: States that a research pipeline drafts and the owner approves, without inventing a byline. Honest, slightly colder.

options.label: Add a byline with a pen name and an avatar
options.commits_to: Google's guidance names fabricated creator profiles, including AI-generated headshots and made-up names, as a deception signal. Not recommended.

decisions.recommendation: A or B. C is the one option the cited guidance explicitly warns against.

sources.ref: Who / How / Why, and the fabricated-authorship warning

decisions.question: Should every page get its own title tag and meta description?

options.label: Yes, write all 21
options.commits_to: A build rule that fails on duplicate descriptions. No policy dimension.

options.label: Only the pages meant to be found in search
options.commits_to: Internal-only pages keep the shared description and are marked noindex so they cannot compete with the articles.

decisions.recommendation: A. Sixteen pages sharing one description is a defect whichever way the site is aimed.

sources.ref: Create unique descriptions for each page on your site

decisions.question: Should the product links carry rel="sponsored"?

options.label: Yes, add the attribute and keep the visible disclosure
options.commits_to: One attribute per link. The visible paid-link label and the Operating Agreement sentence both stay.

options.label: No, leave the links as they are
options.commits_to: Outbound paid links stay unqualified, which Google's guidance treats as a link-spam risk.

decisions.recommendation: A. The cost is one attribute and there is no reader-visible downside.

decisions.question: Will any product be tested, or is this a specification site?

options.label: Test at least one unit per format
options.commits_to: Real purchase or loan, dated notes, original photographs, and a disclosure if any unit was supplied free. Unlocks the language of review.

options.label: Position as a specification and decision tool
options.commits_to: One visible sentence saying no unit was tested, and removal of review vocabulary from the copy. Cheap and honest.

decisions.recommendation: Whichever is chosen, choose it explicitly. The current copy implies evaluation it has not done, which is the weakest position of the three.

sources.ref: Thin affiliation: original reviews and rigorous testing as added value

decisions.question: Should the site publish question-led pages beyond the three products?

options.label: Yes, a small set of distinct question pages
options.commits_to: Each page must answer a different question from existing sourced facts. Guard against volume with no value.

options.label: No, keep the site to the three products
options.commits_to: Six pages total. Easy to keep accurate, hard to attract organic traffic.

decisions.recommendation: A, sized to the questions that can actually be answered from verified facts, not to a page count.

decisions.question: Publish the per-ASIN commission rate once known, or publish no rate at all?

options.label: Publish per-ASIN rates with a read date
options.commits_to: Requires the Associates Central assignment. The 4.50% category quote is replaced by a figure that applies to the actual product.

options.label: Remove the rate discussion from the public pages entirely
options.commits_to: The 4.50% figure moves to the internal analysis page only. Readers see no commission content, which is normal for an affiliate site.
options.effort: One copy change and a rebuild.

decisions.recommendation: B until A is possible. A number that cannot be applied to the product it sits next to invites a wrong calculation.

decisions.question: Should the site be connected to Search Console and given social preview metadata?

options.label: Yes, verify the property and add preview metadata
options.commits_to: The site starts collecting its own impressions and click data, and shared links render with an image. Adds a dependency on an external console.
options.effort: Two to three hours plus verification wait.

options.label: Not yet
options.commits_to: The organic-traffic goal stays unmeasured and unverifiable.

decisions.recommendation: A. Without it, nothing on the site can be shown to have worked.

decisions.question: Should the documentation be corrected and one product name adopted?

options.label: Yes, correct and rename
options.commits_to: Documentation matches the code; one name across the repository.

options.label: Correct the errors, keep the names
options.commits_to: Accuracy fixed; the branding split stays.

decisions.recommendation: A. These are the cheapest credibility fixes on the list.

decisions.question: Should the review page separate open, resolved and historical items?

options.label: Yes, three groups and an accurate KPI
options.commits_to: The review page becomes a work queue rather than an archive.

options.label: Leave one table
options.commits_to: A reviewer keeps reading 38 rows to find the 28 that are unresolved.

sources.ref: The flag register this page renders

decisions.question: Should the copy be rewritten to take positions, or stay strictly descriptive?

options.label: Rewrite with judgement, guarded by the fact rule
options.commits_to: The writer may conclude and rank within verified facts; every factual claim still needs a fact row and the build still fails without one.
options.reversible: Yes, at the cost of the writing time.

options.label: Keep the descriptive style
options.commits_to: The site stays accurate, complete and unreadable. Readers get no answer to the question they arrived with.

decisions.recommendation: A. This is the single biggest factor in whether the site reads as a real publication or as output.

sources.ref: Originality and insight beyond the obvious

decisions.question: Are the three supplied links the intended products? (Ported from the parallel session's worksheet, item D-01.)

options.label: Confirm all three resolved ASINs
options.commits_to: The site keeps publishing these three records. The ASIN, not the short-link token, is treated as the product identifier.

options.label: Replace any link with the intended product's official tagged link
options.commits_to: A new product record has to be verified from its official page before anything is published about it.
options.effort: One verification pass per replaced product.

decisions.recommendation: A, unless one of the three was supplied in error. Confirming the resolved ASINs before publishing campaigns is the parallel session's recommendation and this register adopts it.

decisions.question: Which Associates marketplace and tracking ID should receive purchases? (Ported; item D-02 in the parallel worksheet.)

options.label: Verify the current links inside Associates Central
options.commits_to: If a tag is present but invisible in the resolved URL, the earning claim is already valid and only needs evidence.

options.label: Generate and substitute official tagged links for the chosen marketplace
options.commits_to: Three new Special Links and a rebuild; the earning claim becomes true.

decisions.recommendation: Do not rely on earnings attribution until the three final links are confirmed in the account and tested. This is the parallel session's recommendation and this register adopts it, and it is the same conclusion as D-01.

decisions.question: What research automation is authorised, and from what source may it read? (Ported; item D-03 in the parallel worksheet.)

options.label: Keep research manual and publish only reviewed facts
options.commits_to: The current mode. Slow, but no clause is strained.

options.label: Confirm eligibility and terms, then use the authorised API scope
options.commits_to: Depends on the qualifying-sales prerequisite (Q-02) and on each displayed field being permitted.

options.label: Obtain Amazon's express written approval before any otherwise restricted agent or model use
options.commits_to: A written permission, which is the only route that removes the doubt rather than narrowing it.

decisions.recommendation: Keep automation disabled for Program Content until the applicable terms and any written approvals are confirmed, and never train or improve models with Program Content without the required approval. Ported from the parallel worksheet.

sources.ref: Conditions of Use, License and Access

decisions.question: What measurement is acceptable, and what privacy or consent review is needed before scaling it? (Ported; item D-07 in the parallel worksheet.)

options.label: Keep browser-local, manual reporting only
options.commits_to: The tracker stays as it is: no network call, no attributed figure, no consent question because nothing leaves the device.

options.label: Add first-party measurement only after privacy and legal review
options.commits_to: A documented retention period, a consent basis and a privacy notice before any server-side tool is installed.
options.reversible: Partly; collected data cannot be uncollected.

decisions.recommendation: Keep the current local-only approach until the audience and applicable obligations are known, and do not describe clicks as sales or conversions. Ported from the parallel worksheet.
